adjudication_records.issue_text: onEnable() can be silently skipped when the dialog is dismissed without the Close button in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx (~line 138/265), leaving stale switch state and skipping resetState(), so reopening shows a stale DisplayBackupCodes step with a now-irrelevant blob URL

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, a successful enable no longer calls onEnable() immediately; it only does `setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes)` (handleEnable success path). The only place onEnable() is invoked afterward is the “Close” button inside the DisplayBackupCodes step. If the dialog is dismissed via other mechanisms (Dialog `onOpenChange`, overlay click/ESC, header close, etc.), the component has no handler that calls `resetState()`/revokes `backupCodesUrl` or triggers `onEnable()`, so state can remain on DisplayBackupCodes and the parent may not update the switch/UI to reflect that 2FA is enabled.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Setup endpoint (apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts ~line 60-66) generates, persists, and returns backup codes before TOTP is verified/enabled, silently invalidating previously issued codes if setup is abandoned and re-run

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, the setup handler now generates `backupCodes` (`crypto.randomBytes...`), persists them immediately to `user.backupCodes` via `prisma.user.update(...)`, and returns them in the setup response (`return res.json({ ..., backupCodes })`) while still setting `twoFactorEnabled: false`. This means re-running setup (or abandoning and later re-running) will overwrite the previously issued/stored backup codes before any TOTP verification/enable step occurs, silently invalidating any codes the user may have saved from the prior setup attempt.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Used backup code array in next-auth-options.ts (~line 148-152) never reports 'missing' once exhausted — an array of nulls is still non-null, so MissingBackupCodes never fires and the user gets IncorrectBackupCode forever

adjudication.rationale: In `next-auth-options.ts`, backup-code login only throws `MissingBackupCodes` when `user.backupCodes` is falsy (`if (!user.backupCodes) ...`). After using a backup code it sets the used entry to `null` and re-encrypts the array (`backupCodes[index] = null; ... symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), ...)`). If all codes are used, the stored value is still a non-empty JSON array of `null`s, so `!user.backupCodes` won’t trigger; subsequent attempts will fail `indexOf(...)` and always throw `IncorrectBackupCode`. That matches the finding, but it’s an edge-case/error-reporting semantics issue rather than a functional/security break.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-atomic backup code consumption (race) in next-auth-options.ts (~line 145-158): two concurrent login submissions with the same code can both read it as valid before either write lands, allowing replay of a single backup code

Throwing raw Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError) in the disable API route (~line 47-50) produces a non-JSON 500 HTML page, causing client response.json() to throw and masking the actual server misconfiguration

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the new backup-code branch does `throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError)` when `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is missing. The diff does not show any surrounding `try/catch` converting thrown errors to a JSON response, so this would fall through to Next.js’ default 500 handling (typically an HTML error page). On the client, `DisableTwoFactorModal` unconditionally does `await response.json()` for non-200 responses, which would then throw on a non-JSON 500 response and mask the real misconfiguration.

adjudication_records.issue_text: JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...)) is unguarded in auth-critical paths (disable.ts ~line 56, next-auth-options.ts ~line 134), so corrupt/mismatched encrypted backupCodes throws unhandled errors hiding the root cause

adjudication.rationale: In both auth-critical flows the diff adds `const backupCodes = JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, ...))` without any guarding/try-catch (API route `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` and credentials auth in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`). If `user.backupCodes` decrypts to invalid JSON (e.g., corrupted data, wrong/rotated key, partial write), `JSON.parse` will throw and bubble as an unhandled exception, causing a 500/login failure rather than a controlled `ErrorCode.InternalServerError`/actionable response.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup code length validation comments in BackupCode.tsx (~lines 21-23) are inverted: minLength={10} applies to the raw input, so a 9-char code with dash passes validation and can never match server-side; also HTML attributes are spread onto the component rather than RHF rules so no form-level enforcement validates the code shape

adjudication.rationale: In `BackupCode.tsx`, `minLength={10}` / `maxLength={11}` are just input props and no `register("backupCode", { ...rules })` validation is provided, so react-hook-form itself won’t enforce a specific backup-code shape. Also, because `minLength` counts the raw input, malformed patterns like `"XXXX-XXXXX"` (10 chars incl. dash, 9 after dash removal) would satisfy `minLength` yet will never match the server’s 10-char stored codes (server strips `-` before comparison). However, this is primarily a client-side validation/UX gap (the server correctly rejects invalid codes), and the finding’s “comments are inverted”/“can never match” is overstated since undashed 10-char input would match.

matched_golden_ids: Object URL for backup codes is not revoked on component unmount, leading to a potential memory leak. This can cause increased memory usage over time, especially if the component is mounted and unmounted frequently.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags that the backupCodesUrl Blob/Object URL is not revoked on dialog dismissal/component unmount, only when replaced, which is the same memory-leak concern described in the golden comment.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup codes regenerated and old ones silently invalidated on every setup call in setup.ts (~line 60); codes should only be generated at the /enable step or when !user.backupCodes

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, the endpoint now unconditionally generates `backupCodes` (`Array.from(...crypto.randomBytes...)`) and persists them to `user.backupCodes` on every setup call (`prisma.user.update({ data: { backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(...) } })`). This will overwrite any previously generated (but not yet used) backup codes, so earlier codes a user may have copied/downloaded become invalid if `/setup` is called again. Whether this is undesirable is product/flow-dependent (regenerating on re-setup may be intended), so it’s a concrete design/edge-case concern rather than a clearly verifiable defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Plaintext backup codes returned in the setup response and persisted even if 2FA is never enabled; generation should be deferred to the enable transaction

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts` generating backup codes (`crypto.randomBytes...`) and persisting them immediately in `user.backupCodes` (encrypted) while also leaving `twoFactorEnabled: false`, and returning the plaintext `backupCodes` in the JSON response (`return res.json({ ..., backupCodes })`). This means backup codes can be created/stored even if the user never completes the later enable step, matching the finding. It’s a product/security/flow concern (when to generate/commit codes), not a clearly broken behavior in this diff by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-string backupCode (e.g. object or array) passes truthiness check and crashes the disable endpoint's replaceAll call with an unhandled 500 instead of a 400

adjudication.rationale: In the disable endpoint, the new branch `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode)` treats any truthy `backupCode` as valid input and then unconditionally calls `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll(...)` (apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts). If a client submits a non-string JSON value (e.g., object/array), this will throw a TypeError because `replaceAll` is not defined, resulting in an unhandled 500 instead of a controlled 400. The diff adds no type/shape validation for `backupCode` before using string methods.

adjudication_records.issue_text: throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError) in the disable endpoint API handler when CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY is missing yields an unhandled 500 with non-JSON body, inconsistent with the rest of the flow's JSON error handling

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, when `user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode` and `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is missing, the handler does `throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError)` instead of returning `res.status(...).json(...)`. There is no surrounding try/catch in the diff, so this will bubble to Next.js default error handling (500) and likely not return the JSON `{ error: ... }` shape used elsewhere in this endpoint (e.g., `IncorrectPassword`, `MissingBackupCodes`, etc.), breaking consistent client-side error handling.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Modal state including plaintext backup codes not reset when the EnableTwoFactorModal dialog is dismissed via onOpenChange (X button / outside click); resetState should also run in onOpenChange

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, the Dialog receives `onOpenChange={onOpenChange}` directly, and `resetState()` is only called from the Cancel button handler and the “Close” button in the backup-codes step. If the modal is dismissed via the Dialog’s built-in close mechanisms (X button / outside click triggering `onOpenChange(false)`), no reset occurs, so component state like `backupCodes`/`backupCodesUrl` (and other setup state) can persist across dismiss/reopen. This matches the finding that reset should also run on `onOpenChange` when closing.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Used backup code consumed before the rest of the login flow completes in next-auth-options.ts (~line 145-155); a later failure in authorize burns the code without granting access, potentially locking out a lost-authenticator user

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, when `user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode`, the code is immediately consumed by mutating the decrypted array (`backupCodes[index] = null`) and persisting it via `prisma.user.update(...)` before the `authorize` function has completed successfully (i.e., before it returns the user). Any subsequent error/throw in `authorize` after this block (or failure paths that occur after the DB write) would result in a one-time backup code being burned without a successful login, which can lock out users relying on backup codes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blob object URL leak in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx: URL.createObjectURL(textBlob) is never revoked on modal close or unmount, leaking blob URLs and their backing Blobs in the long-lived SPA session

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx a Blob URL is created via `setBackupCodesUrl(URL.createObjectURL(textBlob))`. The code only revokes the previous URL when creating a new one (`if (backupCodesUrl) URL.revokeObjectURL(backupCodesUrl);`), but `resetState()` (called on cancel/close) does not revoke the current `backupCodesUrl`, nor is there any unmount cleanup shown. In an SPA this leaves at least the last created object URL (and its backing Blob) alive after the modal closes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup codes regenerated and overwritten on every /setup call (setup.ts:60-66), invalidating previously issued codes and causing wasted encrypt+DB-write cycles on abandoned or repeated setup attempts

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, every successful `/setup` call generates a fresh `backupCodes` array (`crypto.randomBytes...`) and immediately persists it via `prisma.user.update({ data: { backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(...) ... } })`. This means repeated/abandoned setup attempts will overwrite the previously generated (and returned) backup codes and perform unnecessary encrypt+DB writes even if 2FA is never ultimately enabled. While this may be an acceptable design choice, it is a concrete side-effect/edge-case concern grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: onEnable callback contract changed in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx: dismissing the dialog via onOpenChange (X, Escape, backdrop) never fires onEnable, desyncing UI state from actual 2FA state after server-side enable

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx, successful enable no longer calls onEnable immediately (changed to `setStep(SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes)` and `return;`). onEnable is only invoked by the explicit “close” button in the DisplayBackupCodes step. The modal is still closable via `<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={onOpenChange}>`, but there is no handler that calls `onEnable()` (or even `resetState()`) when the dialog is dismissed via onOpenChange (X/Escape/backdrop). If the server-side enable succeeded and the user closes the dialog through those mechanisms, the parent UI may never be notified via onEnable, causing state desync.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Setup endpoint (totp/setup.ts) regenerates and overwrites backupCodes on every call, silently invalidating previously issued backup codes

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, each request generates a fresh `backupCodes` array (`crypto.randomBytes...`) and immediately persists it via `prisma.user.update({ data: { backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(...) ... } })` with no check for existing codes. That means any subsequent call to `/totp/setup` overwrites prior stored backup codes, making previously issued/saved codes invalid without any explicit regeneration step or warning.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disable endpoint (totp/disable.ts) doesn't consume the used backup code and assumes a dense string array while the login path replaces used codes with null, causing schema drift on user.backupCodes

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the disable flow *does* “consume” backup codes by clearing them entirely when 2FA is disabled (`data: { backupCodes: null, twoFactorEnabled: false, ... }`). It also doesn’t require a dense string array: it only does `backupCodes.indexOf(<string>)`, and existing `null` entries (as written by the login path in `next-auth-options.ts`) don’t break this lookup or parsing. So the claimed drift/bug (not consuming + dense-array assumption causing issues) isn’t supported by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Setup response returns plaintext backup codes before the second factor is verified, exposing live credentials to any caller confirming the password

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup` now generates and returns `backupCodes` in the JSON response (`return res.json({ secret, keyUri, dataUri, backupCodes });`) and the client stores them immediately on successful setup (`setBackupCodes(body.backupCodes);`). This happens before the subsequent enable step (`/enable`) verifies the TOTP. That said, returning secrets during setup is part of the intended 2FA enrollment flow (it already returns the TOTP `secret`/QR), so this is more of a security/flow design concern (e.g., prefer generating/returning backup codes only after successful TOTP verification) than a clear functional defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: New locale keys added only to en/common.json, so non-English users see raw translation keys in login page and 2FA modals

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds new translation keys only in `apps/web/public/static/locales/en/common.json` (e.g. `backup_code`, `backup_codes`, `lost_access`, `incorrect_backup_code`, `missing_backup_codes`). The new UI uses these keys via `t(...)` in `BackupCode.tsx`, `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx`, `DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx`, and `login.tsx`, but the diff shows no corresponding additions to other locale JSON files. Whether users see raw keys depends on the i18n fallback behavior (not shown), but the change is clearly incomplete for non-English locales.

adjudication_records.issue_text: TwoFactorAuthAPI.disable signature changed to a mandatory third backupCode parameter without making it optional for backward compatibility

adjudication.rationale: The diff does change `TwoFactorAuthAPI.disable` to require a third `backupCode` parameter, but the only call site shown (`DisableTwoFactorModal`) is updated to pass `backupCode`, so there’s no verifiable broken behavior in this PR. The claim about needing backward compatibility isn’t grounded in the diff (it’s an internal helper module, and no other callers are shown).

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup-code consumption in next-auth-options.ts is not atomic: concurrent login attempts can both read the unmodified codes list and reuse the same single-use backup code (TOCTOU)
matched_golden_ids: Because backupCodes are decrypted and mutated in memory before being written back, two concurrent login requests using the same backupCode could both pass this check and update, so a single backup code may effectively be accepted more than once if used concurrently, weakening the intended one-time-use semantics.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: Both describe a race condition/TOCTOU where backup code consumption is not atomic: concurrent login requests can read the same unconsumed backupCodes, both pass validation, and both update, allowing a supposedly one-time backup code to be accepted more than once.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup code is consumed before the rest of authorize() completes, so a failure after the update permanently burns the code without granting a session

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, the backup-code branch validates and then immediately persists consumption by updating `users.backupCodes` (`await prisma.user.update(...)` after setting `backupCodes[index] = null`). This happens inside `authorize()` before NextAuth finishes the sign-in flow (session/JWT/callbacks are outside this function). If anything throws after this DB update (within remaining `authorize()` logic not shown, or in subsequent NextAuth processing), the backup code has already been irreversibly consumed without guaranteeing a session was established, effectively “burning” the code on a failed login.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup codes generated at setup are never shown if the user closes EnableTwoFactorModal via onOpenChange (X/Esc), and there is no UI to regenerate them without disabling and re-enabling 2FA

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, backup codes are only rendered in the new SetupStep.DisplayBackupCodes UI (and are set from /totp/setup response), but there is no other UI/flow in this diff to re-display or regenerate backup codes later (generation only happens in /api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts; no “regenerate/view backup codes” path is added). Also, the modal’s Dialog uses `onOpenChange={onOpenChange}` without invoking `resetState()`/`onEnable()` on close via X/Esc, so if the parent unmounts the modal on close, the user could lose the one in-modal chance to copy/download codes. This is a concrete UX/flow gap introduced by the change rather than a strictly provable runtime defect from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Aborted 2FA setup attempts silently overwrite previously generated backup codes

adjudication.rationale: In `/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, every call generates a fresh `backupCodes` array and immediately persists it via `prisma.user.update({ data: { backupCodes: ... } })` before 2FA is actually enabled. If the user abandons the enable flow and later restarts setup, the newly generated codes will overwrite whatever was stored from a prior setup attempt, with no explicit warning or recovery path shown in this diff. However, because backup codes are only used when `twoFactorEnabled` is true (see next-auth authorize/disable logic), overwriting during an incomplete setup doesn’t necessarily break correctness for an actively enabled 2FA account based on what’s shown here—so it’s more of a flow/state-management concern than a clearly demonstrated defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: setup.ts persists encrypted backup codes without checking CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY, unlike login and disable.ts, causing 500s or undecryptable codes when the key is missing

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, the PR adds `backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY)` with no guard for a missing `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY`. By contrast, both `next-auth-options.ts` (backup code login) and `totp/disable.ts` explicitly check for the key before decrypting/using backup codes and return/throw errors when it’s missing. If the env var is undefined, `symmetricEncrypt(...)` may throw at setup time (500) or store data that later cannot be decrypted reliably, breaking backup code functionality.

adjudication_records.issue_text: disable.ts throws Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError) instead of returning a JSON error, so the frontend's response.json() fails and the missing-encryption-key signal is swallowed client-side

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the new backup-code branch does `throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError)` when `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is missing, instead of `return res.status(...).json(...)`. This is inconsistent with the rest of the handler which returns JSON errors (e.g., IncorrectPassword, MissingBackupCodes). On the client (`DisableTwoFactorModal.handleDisable`), non-200 responses are parsed via `await response.json()`, so an unhandled throw can lead to a non-JSON 500 response and `response.json()` failing, causing the specific error signal to be lost and falling into the generic catch path.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Unguarded JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(user.backupCodes, ...)) in next-auth-options.ts and disable.ts crashes with an unstructured 500 / InternalServerError on corrupt or unparseable ciphertext, locking users out of 2FA recovery

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds backup-code support and introduces unguarded `JSON.parse(symmetricDecrypt(...))` in both `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` (authorize backup-code path) and `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` (backup-code disable path). If `user.backupCodes` contains corrupt/unparseable ciphertext, `symmetricDecrypt` or `JSON.parse` will throw, and in the API route that will bubble to an unstructured 500 rather than returning a typed `{ error: ErrorCode.* }` response. This can prevent login/2FA disable via backup codes for affected users.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup code comparison is case/format sensitive: no lowercase/trim normalization on either server or client (BackupCode.tsx sends raw input), so uppercase input fails
matched_golden_ids: Backup code validation is case-sensitive due to the use of indexOf(). This causes validation to fail if a user enters uppercase hex characters, as backup codes should be case-insensitive for a better user experience.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate identifies that backup code validation/comparison is case-sensitive and that uppercase hex input fails due to lack of normalization, matching the golden issue about needing case-insensitive validation for better UX.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Blob object URL in EnableTwoFactorModal is never revoked if the modal unmounts or the user closes after setup, leaking memory

adjudication.rationale: In `EnableTwoFactorModal`, a Blob URL is created via `URL.createObjectURL(textBlob)` and only the *previous* URL is revoked when generating a new one (`if (backupCodesUrl) URL.revokeObjectURL(backupCodesUrl);`). There is no cleanup on modal close/unmount (no `useEffect` return cleanup, and `resetState()` does not revoke or clear `backupCodesUrl`), so the last created object URL can persist and leak memory.

adjudication_records.issue_text: E2E test login.2fa.e2e.ts uses expect(...).toBeTruthy() on isChecked() which always passes when the locator resolves, so the 2FA enable state is not actually verified; backup-code happy path also unverified

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows the E2E test using `await expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch]').isChecked()).toBeTruthy();` and even includes an inline `// FIXME: this passes even when switch is not checked` comment, indicating the assertion is not reliably verifying the enable state. The newly added backup-code flow is also only partially exercised: the test clicks download/copy/close but leaves `// TODO: check file content` and `// TODO: check clipboard content`, so the happy-path correctness of generated/formatting backup codes isn’t actually validated.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No e2e test for backup-code login flow: valid code login, single-use replay rejection, MissingBackupCodes exhaustion path, and dashed vs undashed input matching are all untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds substantial new backup-code auth behavior but only extends Playwright coverage to displaying/download/copy/close of backup codes after enabling 2FA (apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts) and even includes a TODO to add more backup code tests. Backup-code login and single-use consumption logic is implemented in next-auth authorize (packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts: checks credentials.backupCode, matches after replaceAll("-", ""), then sets used code to null and re-encrypts), and new error paths (IncorrectBackupCode, MissingBackupCodes) are surfaced in the login UI (apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx). None of the requested flows (valid backup-code login, replay rejection due to nulling, MissingBackupCodes when user.backupCodes is null, dashed vs undashed matching) are covered by e2e tests in this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup-code single-use invalidation (nulling used code and re-encrypting) has no unit or e2e test; a regression like off-by-one index or encrypting before removal would silently allow code reuse

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds single-use backup code invalidation in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` (when `user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode`, it finds `index`, then does `backupCodes[index] = null;` and persists via `prisma.user.update` with `symmetricEncrypt(...)`). The added Playwright test `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts` only exercises displaying/downloading/copying backup codes after enabling 2FA and even includes a TODO to add backup code tests; it does not cover logging in with a backup code nor ensuring reuse fails. No unit tests are added around this invalidation logic, so regressions in index selection or persistence order could go unnoticed.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Disable-2FA-with-backup-code path untested: distinct error branches (IncorrectBackupCode, MissingBackupCodes), TOTP-check skip when backup code used, empty-string falsiness routing, and the 'lost access' toggle-back flow all lack coverage

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds nontrivial new backup-code flows for disabling 2FA and login, including new error branches and conditional routing, but the only Playwright additions test the *enable* flow’s backup-code display/copy/download (apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts). There is even an explicit TODO about adding backup code tests. The new disable endpoint has distinct branches for IncorrectBackupCode and MissingBackupCodes and skips TOTP verification when `req.body.backupCode` is truthy (apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts), and UI toggles between TOTP and backup code inputs via the `twoFactorLostAccess` state (DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx and login.tsx) with form-reset behavior. None of these new disable/login backup-code branches (including the truthy check behavior for empty string) are covered by tests in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Download test only asserts suggestedFilename, not blob content matching displayed codes; clipboard test asserts a toast rather than actual copied data, so formatBackupCode slicing bugs would pass

adjudication.rationale: In the new Playwright flow (apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts), the download assertion only checks `download.suggestedFilename()` and explicitly leaves `// TODO: check file content`, and the copy assertion only waits for `toast-success` with `// TODO: check clipboard content`. Since the UI and blob/clipboard both depend on `formatBackupCode` in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx, a formatting/slicing regression could slip through without these stronger assertions. This is a concrete test coverage gap, not a product defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Known vacuous assertion isChecked()).toBeTruthy() left in place with only a FIXME instead of being fixed to use data-state="checked"

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts`, the new FIXME highlights a real issue that remains unfixed: `await expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch]').isChecked()).toBeTruthy();` passes a Promise (or non-awaited result) into `expect`, making the assertion effectively vacuous/truthy regardless of the switch state. The diff itself even notes it “passes even when switch is not checked” and suggests the correct approach (`data-state="checked"`), which is already used later in the test but not here.

adjudication_records.issue_text: setup endpoint overwrites backupCodes on every call before 2FA is enabled, silently invalidating a previously displayed batch on double-setup and leaving codes when twoFactorEnabled is false; neither behavior is tested

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, each successful setup call generates a fresh `backupCodes` array and immediately persists it to the user (`backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(...)`) while also explicitly setting `twoFactorEnabled: false`. This means repeated calls to the setup endpoint before enabling 2FA will overwrite any previously generated/displayed backup codes, and backup codes can remain stored even if 2FA never gets enabled. The diff also doesn’t add coverage for this lifecycle/edge-case (the added Playwright test only checks download/copy/close UI, not repeated setup or abort flows). While this is a real, diff-grounded concern, it’s not clearly a functional defect given backup codes are only accepted when `twoFactorEnabled` is true (e.g., in `next-auth-options.ts` and `totp/disable.ts`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: BackupCode input validation untested: minLength/maxLength attributes assume exact XXXXX-XXXXX format with no normalization test for uppercase, missing dash, or trailing-space variants, causing opaque 'incorrect' errors

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds a new BackupCode input (`apps/web/components/auth/BackupCode.tsx`) with `minLength={10}` and `maxLength={11}` and registers `backupCode` without any normalization (no trim/case handling). On the server, backup codes are matched via `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` in the disable API and `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` in next-auth authorize, but there is no trimming or case-normalization, so variants like trailing spaces or uppercase would fail and surface only as `IncorrectBackupCode`. The added Playwright test explicitly has a TODO about adding backup code tests and does not cover backup-code login/disable flows, so the validation/normalization behavior is indeed untested.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test builder mock only adds backupCodes: null default with no helper for encrypted backup codes, forcing all backup-code testing to e2e level and leaving the encryption round-trip untested

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds `backupCodes: null` to the default test user builder (`packages/lib/test/builder.ts`), but does not add any builder helper/util to generate/encrypt backup codes matching the new logic that uses `symmetricEncrypt/symmetricDecrypt` (e.g., `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` and `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`). This is a concrete gap in test scaffolding that makes it harder to write unit/integration tests for the backup-code encryption/decryption path and encourages relying on higher-level e2e tests instead.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Duplicated backup-code verification logic in disable.ts:46-67 and next-auth-options.ts:131-152 (encryption-key check, MissingBackupCodes check, decrypt, dash-stripping, indexOf lookup) will drift; extract into a shared helper in @calcom/features/auth/lib

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows essentially the same backup-code verification flow implemented twice: in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` (encryption key presence check, `MissingBackupCodes`, decrypt+`JSON.parse`, dash stripping via `replaceAll("-", "")`, `indexOf` lookup) and again in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` within `authorize` (same checks and lookup). This is a concrete maintainability/architecture concern introduced by the change: the logic can diverge (it already differs in side effects—`next-auth-options.ts` nulls out a used code and re-encrypts, while `disable.ts` does not), so extracting a shared helper would reduce drift risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Inconsistent guard on CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY: setup.ts:66 calls symmetricEncrypt with no missing-key check, unlike disable.ts and next-auth-options.ts, which can throw or silently produce unusable data

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, the new code stores `backupCodes` via `symmetricEncrypt(JSON.stringify(backupCodes), process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY)` without checking that `CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` is set. In contrast, the new/updated backup-code paths in `totp/disable.ts` and `next-auth-options.ts` explicitly guard against a missing key and return/throw a controlled error. If the key is unset, `setup.ts` can throw at encryption time or persist unusable encrypted data, leading to broken 2FA setup/backup-code flows.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup codes persisted before 2FA is actually enabled: setup.ts:57-66 stores and silently regenerates backupCodes on every setup call, invalidating previously saved codes without warning

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, backup codes are generated unconditionally (`const backupCodes = ...`) and then persisted on every setup call via `prisma.user.update({ data: { backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(...) } })`, even though `twoFactorEnabled` is explicitly set to `false` in the same update. This means repeated calls to the setup endpoint will overwrite (invalidate) any previously issued backup codes without any server-side guard or warning in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Dead comment inside empty branch in disable.ts:64 misleads readers about where the TOTP path lies; delete it

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the referenced comment is not inside an empty branch: the `if (user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode)` branch performs real logic (encryption key check, missing backup codes check, decrypt + match validation). The comment `// if user has 2fa and NOT using backup code, try totp` is placed immediately before the `else if (user.twoFactorEnabled)` TOTP path, so it does not mislead about where the TOTP path lies in any verifiable way from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stale state in EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx resetState(): backupCodes, backupCodesUrl, dataUri, secret, and totpCode remain populated, stale blob URL never revoked (leak), old values shown momentarily on failed setup

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx, resetState() only clears password/errorMessage/step, but does not clear other state set during setup: backupCodes, backupCodesUrl, dataUri, and secret. Since backupCodesUrl is created via URL.createObjectURL(...) and only revoked when creating a new one ("if (backupCodesUrl) URL.revokeObjectURL(backupCodesUrl);"), calling resetState() (e.g. on cancel/close) can leave an unreleased blob URL (leak) and stale backup codes/QR state that could flash/show if the modal is reopened without unmounting. Additionally, the react-hook-form totpCode value is never reset in resetState(), so it can remain populated across step resets.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Component name mismatch: BackupCode.tsx:8 exports default function TwoFactor; rename to BackupCode and use a TS type for props instead of implicit any
Duplicated 'lost access' toggle UI/state across login.tsx:104-135 and DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx:103-113; consolidate into a shared hook or component like useTwoFactorModeToggle

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces parallel UI/state patterns for switching between TOTP and backup-code flows in two places: `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx` adds `twoFactorLostAccess` state and footer buttons to toggle modes and clear relevant form fields, while `apps/web/components/settings/DisableTwoFactorModal.tsx` adds its own `twoFactorLostAccess` state, toggle button, and `resetForm` logic to switch between `<TwoFactor />` and `<BackupCode />`. This is a real, diff-grounded duplication/maintainability concern rather than a correctness defect; consolidating into a shared hook/component could reduce divergence risk.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Input normalization asymmetry: BackupCode.tsx:21-22 enforces minLength/maxLength/required on client but server only strips dashes, so whitespace or lowercase hex codes fail; centralize trim + dash-stripping in one shared helper

adjudication.rationale: Backup codes are generated as lowercase hex strings (setup.ts: crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")), but both login authorize and the disable API only normalize by removing dashes (credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "") and req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")) and do not trim whitespace or normalize case. The client TextField only enforces length/required (BackupCode.tsx) and won’t prevent users from pasting codes with leading/trailing spaces or uppercase hex, causing valid codes to be rejected server-side.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup codes compared in non-constant time (indexOf against plaintext codes) in disable.ts:59 and next-auth-options.ts:148 with no hashing; use a consumeBackupCode(userId, code) helper owning storage + comparison

adjudication.rationale: The diff adds backup-code verification by decrypting stored codes and using `Array.indexOf(...)` on the plaintext list (e.g. `disable.ts` checks `backupCodes.indexOf(req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))`, and `next-auth-options.ts` does the same for `credentials.backupCode`). This is an early-exit, non-constant-time comparison and the codes are stored as decryptable plaintext (encrypted, not hashed). As a security-sensitive credential, this is a verifiable weakness introduced by the change; centralizing comparison/consumption in a helper would also avoid duplicated logic between the API route and NextAuth authorize flow.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Test file login.2fa.e2e.ts carries acknowledged gaps: TODO at :12 for more backup code tests, and FIXME at :50 about isChecked assertion passing even when unchecked, weakening the enable e2e test

adjudication.rationale: The diff explicitly introduces/contains test-quality gaps in `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts`: a `// TODO: add more backup code tests, e.g. login + disabling 2fa with backup` comment (newly added near the top) and a `// FIXME: this passes even when switch is not checked...` comment immediately above `expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy();`, acknowledging the assertion is unreliable. These are concrete, diff-grounded issues affecting test coverage/robustness rather than production behavior.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup codes are persisted in setup.ts:60-67 before 2FA is enabled; if the user cancels, codes remain stored, and re-running setup silently overwrites a previously saved set

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts` now generates `backupCodes` and persists them immediately via `prisma.user.update({ data: { backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(...), twoFactorEnabled: false, twoFactorSecret: ... }})` before 2FA is actually enabled. If a user cancels the enable flow after calling setup, those codes remain stored (though unused because backup-code login/disable checks require `user.twoFactorEnabled`). Re-running setup will regenerate and overwrite `backupCodes` in the DB (same update call), which is a real lifecycle/UX concern introduced by this change, even if it may be acceptable behavior rather than a definite correctness bug.

adjudication_records.issue_text: MissingBackupCodes error is unreachable once codes are consumed because used codes are replaced with null in the array, leaving backupCodes non-null; the guard should check for remaining non-null entries

adjudication.rationale: In `next-auth-options.ts`, backup codes are “consumed” by setting `backupCodes[index] = null` and re-encrypting, so `user.backupCodes` remains a non-null JSON string even when all entries are null. The guard `if (!user.backupCodes) throw MissingBackupCodes;` will therefore not trigger once all codes are used; instead the flow falls through to `indexOf(...) === -1` and throws `IncorrectBackupCode`. The same pattern exists in the disable endpoint (`disable.ts`) which only checks `if (!user.backupCodes) return MissingBackupCodes` before searching the array. Thus `MissingBackupCodes` is effectively unreachable when the field exists but contains no remaining non-null codes, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup code is not consumed single-use in the disable flow (disable.ts:64-73); if an error occurs after validation but before the final update, the validated code stays valid

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, when `req.body.backupCode` is provided, the code is only validated (`indexOf(...)`) and then the handler proceeds without consuming/removing that specific backup code. Backup codes are only cleared at the very end via the Prisma update (`data: { backupCodes: null, twoFactorEnabled: false, ... }`). If anything throws/returns an error after validation but before that final update (e.g., DB failure), the validated backup code remains stored and can be reused, violating the intended single-use semantics described in the UI copy.

adjudication_records.issue_text: backupCode field is likely missing from the login form's zod schema (formSchema not updated in apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx:218), so the resolver may strip or reject the backupCode value, breaking lost-access login

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `LoginValues` gaining `backupCode` and the UI toggling between `<TwoFactor>` and `<BackupCode>`, but it does not show the definition of `formSchema` in `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx`. Since the zod schema content isn’t included/changed in this diff, we can’t verify that `backupCode` is missing from it or that the resolver would strip/reject it.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No server-side format validation on backup code input in disable.ts / next-auth-options.ts; server accepts any string and the disable endpoint lacks rate limiting, permitting unlimited brute-force attempts

adjudication.rationale: In both the disable API route and the NextAuth credentials flow, `backupCode` is accepted as an arbitrary string and only normalized via `replaceAll("-", "")` before comparison (`disable.ts`: `req.body.backupCode.replaceAll(...)`, `next-auth-options.ts`: `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll(...)`), with no server-side length/charset validation. Additionally, `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` shows no rate-limiting/throttling around incorrect backup-code attempts (it simply returns `IncorrectBackupCode` on mismatch), so repeated online guessing is not constrained by this endpoint’s code.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup code comparison via indexOf on the decrypted array is not constant-time, creating a potential timing side channel

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces backup-code validation using `indexOf` on a decrypted array in two places: `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` (`const index = backupCodes.indexOf(...)`) and `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts` (`const index = backupCodes.indexOf(...)`). `indexOf` performs an early-exit linear search and the underlying string comparisons are not constant-time, so the check is timing-variable based on where (or whether) a match occurs, which can create a timing side channel as the finding states.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Stale backup codes are silently invalidated on re-setup (setup.ts:60 regenerates codes each call) and the UI never warns users that previously saved codes were regenerated

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, each call generates a fresh `backupCodes` array (`crypto.randomBytes...`) and overwrites `user.backupCodes` in the DB, which necessarily makes any previously saved backup codes unusable. The UI flow in `EnableTwoFactorModal.tsx` displays whatever `body.backupCodes` it just received, but there is no explicit warning/message that prior backup codes (if any) have been replaced/invalidated; the modal only shows generic instructions (`backup_code_instructions`). This is a UX/edge-case concern grounded in the diff, but not a clear correctness defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup codes are displayed exactly once with no regeneration/recovery path; closing the dialog at the DisplayBackupCodes step via onOpenChange skips resetState/onEnable, losing codes forever, and after all 10 codes are consumed user.backupCodes remains the truthy string '[null,null,...]' so the user gets IncorrectBackupCode forever, both leading to permanent lockout

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, after successful enable the flow sets `step` to `DisplayBackupCodes` and only calls `onEnable()` (and `resetState()`) from the explicit “close” button handler (`data-testid="backup-codes-close"`). If the dialog is closed through the generic `Dialog` close mechanism (`onOpenChange`, e.g., overlay/escape/close control), there is no code to invoke `onEnable()` or `resetState()`, so the parent may not be notified and the user may lose the only UI moment where the newly generated `backupCodes` are shown. Separately, in next-auth `authorize`, backup code use sets `backupCodes[index] = null` and re-encrypts the array; when all are consumed the stored `backupCodes` field remains a non-null encrypted string, so `MissingBackupCodes` will never trigger and any future backup code attempt will always fall into `IncorrectBackupCode` (`indexOf(...) === -1`), which is a broken/incorrect terminal state signal and can contribute to lockout if TOTP is unavailable.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Backup code is consumed (burned) before login is guaranteed to succeed — backupCodes[index] = null and DB write happen inside authorize() as soon as the code matches, so a later failure permanently loses the code without granting access; consumption should occur only after the full sign-in transaction succeeds

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`, inside the Credentials provider `authorize()`, when `user.twoFactorEnabled && credentials.backupCode` matches, the code is immediately “burned” via `backupCodes[index] = null` followed by `await prisma.user.update(...)` before the sign-in flow is fully completed. Since `authorize()` runs prior to NextAuth finishing the session/callback pipeline, any later failure (e.g., in subsequent authorize logic not shown here, NextAuth callbacks, or session/token handling after `authorize` returns/throws) could still result in the backup code being permanently consumed without a successful login. The diff clearly shows consumption occurs at match-time rather than at confirmed successful sign-in.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Server-side backup-code validation has case/whitespace mismatch with UI — placeholder 'XXXXX-XXXXX' suggests uppercase but codes are lowercase hex, and there is no .trim().toLowerCase() normalization on client or server, so uppercase or space-padded input fails with a generic error

adjudication.rationale: Backup codes are generated as lowercase hex (`crypto.randomBytes(5).toString("hex")` in `totp/setup.ts`), but both server-side validators compare with a raw `indexOf` after only stripping dashes (`req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` in `totp/disable.ts` and `credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", "")` in `next-auth-options.ts`). The UI placeholder in `BackupCode.tsx` is uppercase (`"XXXXX-XXXXX"`) and there is no `.trim()`/case normalization on client or server, so users entering uppercase or space-padded codes will fail validation. (The error is not always generic—specific IncorrectBackupCode handling exists—but the mismatch/normalization defect is real.)

adjudication_records.issue_text: E2e test uses silent-pass verification: expect(page.locator(...).isChecked()).toBeTruthy() passes even when the switch is not checked, so the suite won't catch 2FA-enable regressions; should use await expect(locator).toBeChecked()

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/playwright/login.2fa.e2e.ts`, the test does `await expect(page.locator('[data-testid=two-factor-switch]').isChecked()).toBeTruthy();`. `isChecked()` returns a Promise, and `toBeTruthy()` will pass on the Promise object itself (truthy) rather than the resolved boolean, making the assertion effectively a silent-pass (the diff even includes a `FIXME` comment noting it passes when not checked). This can let 2FA-enable regressions slip through; it should use `await expect(locator).toBeChecked()` or `await expect(await locator.isChecked()).toBeTruthy()`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: disable.ts throws raw Error with an error-code string instead of returning a response when encryption key is missing — yields 500 with stack trace, while the identical condition in next-auth-options.ts throws from authorize and next-auth translates it to credentials-rejected, so the two paths behave differently for the same misconfiguration

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the new backup-code branch checks `!process.env.CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY` and then does `throw new Error(ErrorCode.InternalServerError);` instead of returning an HTTP error response (e.g., `res.status(500).json(...)`). The diff shows no surrounding try/catch in this handler snippet, so this will bubble as an unhandled exception and produce a generic 500 (and potentially leak stack traces in logs) rather than a controlled JSON error like the other branches that `return res.status(400).json({ error: ... })`.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Non-constant-time backup code comparison using backupCodes.indexOf(...) — String.indexOf short-circuits on first character mismatch, leaking a weak timing oracle on code prefix

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces backup code verification via `backupCodes.indexOf(req.body.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))` in `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts` and similarly `backupCodes.indexOf(credentials.backupCode.replaceAll("-", ""))` in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`. This performs standard JS string equality checks while searching the array, which are not constant-time and can short-circuit on first mismatch, creating a potential (though likely noisy) timing side-channel for a secret value. The finding misnames it as `String.indexOf`, but the underlying non-constant-time comparison issue is grounded in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: No rate limiting on backup-code attempts at the disable endpoint, unlike the login path behind checkRateLimitAndThrowError, allowing unlimited guessing

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable.ts`, the new backup-code branch (`if (user.twoFactorEnabled && req.body.backupCode) { ... }`) performs unlimited comparisons against the decrypted `backupCodes` array and returns specific errors (`IncorrectBackupCode`, `MissingBackupCodes`) without any visible rate limiting or throttling in this handler. The diff does show the login/auth path has infrastructure for rate limiting (`checkRateLimitAndThrowError` is imported in `packages/features/auth/lib/next-auth-options.ts`), but no analogous protection is added to the disable endpoint, so backup-code guessing attempts against `/api/auth/two-factor/totp/disable` appear unbounded based on this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: EnableTwoFactorModal has stale state on dialog close/reopen — resetState() is only invoked from Cancel and Close buttons, never from onOpenChange/onCancel, so reopening resumes at DisplayBackupCodes/EnterTotpCode with a stale blob URL and the password lingering in component memory

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, local state (step/password/backupCodesUrl) is only reset via resetState() in the Cancel button handler and the backup-codes Close handler. The Dialog is rendered as `<Dialog open={open} onOpenChange={onOpenChange}>` but there is no effect or wrapper on `onOpenChange` to call resetState when the dialog is closed by other means (e.g., backdrop click / Esc / parent toggling `open` to false). Since the component keeps state in `useState` (`step`, `password`, `backupCodes`, `backupCodesUrl`), reopening can resume at a later step with stale values; additionally, `backupCodesUrl` is only revoked when creating a new one, not on close/unmount, and `password` remains in memory unless resetState runs.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Setup stores backup codes even if 2FA is never enabled — backupCodes is persisted in the same prisma.user.update that regenerates the TOTP secret at the password-confirm step, so every setup attempt silently overwrites previously saved codes; codes should be generated at enable time

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/api/auth/two-factor/totp/setup.ts`, backup codes are generated and persisted immediately during the setup (password-confirm/QR step): `const backupCodes = ...;` then `prisma.user.update({ data: { backupCodes: symmetricEncrypt(...), twoFactorEnabled: false, twoFactorSecret: ... }})`. This means a setup attempt writes/overwrites `users.backupCodes` even before 2FA is actually enabled (the enable flow happens later), and repeated setup attempts will replace any previously stored backup codes. However, from the diff alone this doesn’t clearly cause broken behavior/security (backup codes are only accepted when `user.twoFactorEnabled` is true), so it’s more of a flow/architecture concern than a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Switching between TOTP and backup code in login loses error context / allows mode-confusion submission — toggle handlers clear the opposite field asymmetrically, so a stale backupCode left from a prior failed attempt can be submitted and shadow a freshly typed TOTP code, sending the user down the backup branch with the old code

adjudication.rationale: In `apps/web/pages/auth/login.tsx`, the toggle handlers explicitly clear the *other* credential when switching modes: entering backup mode (`setTwoFactorLostAccess(true)`) calls `methods.setValue("totpCode", "")`, and returning from backup mode (`twoFactorLostAccess` branch of the go-back handler) calls `methods.setValue("backupCode", "")`. This prevents a stale `backupCode` from remaining set when the TOTP UI is shown, so the claimed “stale backupCode shadowing a freshly typed TOTP code” is not evidenced by the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Object URL leak in EnableTwoFactorModal — blob URL is revoked only when a previous URL exists and never on unmount, so each abandoned setup leaks a blob: URL

adjudication.rationale: In EnableTwoFactorModal, a Blob URL is created via `URL.createObjectURL(textBlob)` and stored in `backupCodesUrl`. The code only revokes the *previous* URL when creating a new one (`if (backupCodesUrl) URL.revokeObjectURL(backupCodesUrl);`), but there is no cleanup on modal close/reset (`resetState` doesn’t revoke or clear `backupCodesUrl`) and no unmount effect to revoke it. If the user completes setup (URL created) and then closes/cancels/unmounts without creating another URL, that object URL is never revoked.

adjudication_records.issue_text: Misleading component name in BackupCode.tsx — export default function TwoFactor(...) in a file named BackupCode.tsx invites import mistakes; also minLength/maxLength on TextField may be overridden because {...methods.register("backupCode")} is spread after the explicit props so RHF's props win on collision
matched_golden_ids: The exported function TwoFactor handles backup codes and is in BackupCode.tsx. Inconsistent naming.
adjudication_records.primary_judge_reasoning: The candidate flags the same core issue as the golden comment: a function/component exported as `TwoFactor` residing in `BackupCode.tsx`, creating inconsistent/misleading naming and potential import confusion. It additionally mentions a separate RHF prop-collision concern, but that doesn’t negate the primary match.
